Elena P: hey folks — first week here, trying to switch to the 'redwood-dev' context and access my team's namespace, but I get a permissions error. any quick pointers?
Ben (DevEx): welcome Elena! can you paste the exact error and the output of `kubectl config current-context` and `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n <namespace>`?
Elena P: sure — current context shows `redwood-dev-cluster`, and when i run `kubectl get pods -n rl-frontend` i get:
```
Error from server (Forbidden): pods is forbidden: User "system:serviceaccount:default:elena-sa" cannot list resource "pods" in API group "" in the namespace "rl-frontend"
```
Ben (DevEx): ok that indicates your service account (elena-sa) doesn't have RBAC for that namespace. are you using the shared dev kubeconfig or the onboarding service account?
Elena P: i followed the onboarding doc and swapped into the service account via `kubectl config set-credentials elena --token=...` — maybe that's the problem?
Priya R: tagging infra — @Sam K can you confirm whether rl-frontend is locked down to a team role?
Sam K: looks like rl-frontend has a NamespaceRoleBinding that grants `team-frontend` rights. new hires should be added to `team-frontend` group via our identity sync. i'll open an infra ticket. infra-bot: Created ticket INFRA-4721 to add elena-sa to group team-frontend (priority: low).
Elena P: thanks — is there a temporary way for me to test other clusters/namespaces in the meantime?
Ben (DevEx): you can `kubectl config use-context redwood-dev-cluster` and try `kubectl get namespaces` — but if your SA lacks list permissions you'll see similar errors. For quick dev testing, we usually create a personal namespace `dev-elena` and bind `edit` role to your SA. Sam, could you provision `dev-elena` until INFRA-4721 is done?
Sam K: yep, will create `dev-elena` and bind edit to elena-sa in ~10m. i'll post here when done.
Elena P: awesome, appreciate it! any docs i should read to avoid this next time?
Ben (DevEx): check the onboarding page: https://redwood.dev/onboarding/k8s-access — sections on kubeconfig, SA impersonation, and the identity sync flow. short checklist: (1) confirm context with `kubectl config current-context`, (2) run `kubectl auth can-i <verb> <resource> -n <ns>`, (3) if 403, ping infra or open INFRA ticket, (4) request a personal namespace for dev work.
Elena P: thanks, saved — feel much better. :rocket:
Sam K: done — dev namespace `dev-elena` created and `edit` bound to elena-sa. try `kubectl get pods -n dev-elena` now.
Elena P: works! can see an empty namespace. i'll deploy the sample app. thanks all :slightly_smiling_face:
